player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly assumed that the pronoun "she" must refer to the patient because the patient is the subject of the first clause, ignoring the possibility that the specialist could also be female and possess the condition. In ambiguous pronoun resolution tasks, I should not rely solely on grammatical proximity or narrative logic; instead, I must explicitly evaluate if the sentence structure allows for multiple valid antecedents. Next time, I will analyze whether the verb phrase "had a rare skin condition" logically applies to both potential referents (the patient and the specialist). If both are plausible, I will select option (C) Ambiguous rather than forcing a single interpretation based on assumption.
